target_customer: Operations teams at document-heavy enterprises (mortgage and lending, banking, insurance, healthcare, manufacturing) and, for the Workforce product, teams of 2 to 50
problem: Manual back-office work and brittle legacy RPA scripts break when screens or documents change. Automat sells agents that operate computers the way people do and self-heal.
business_model: Managed enterprise automation with a forward-deployed engineering team, plus per-agent Workforce subscriptions
product_category: Agentic process automation (AI-driven RPA and document processing)

founders.name: Lucas Ochoa
education: Carnegie Mellon University School of Design alumnus; technical foundation from CMU School of Computer Science classes (degree not named)
founders.background_notes: Sources: CMU School of Design article and the Automat Series A blog post. He saw that physical and software robots rely on similar underlying technology.

founders.name: Gautam Bose
prior_employers: Google (Chrome and Google Cloud transformer experiments, LLM research teams)
education: Carnegie Mellon University, BDes 2019 (School of Design)
founders.background_notes: The two met at Google X per the company blog.

technical_complexity.rationale: At the start in 2023 the product was RPA for Chrome built on GPT-3 and computer vision (YC launch post title). Reliable self-healing UI agents that recover from errors were hard, but the pieces were available through LLM APIs.

defensibility.rationale: Model capability is rented from third parties and many teams could build agent wrappers. Forward-deployed engineers who build and monitor every automation create some customer lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The company's own comparison pages name UiPath, Automation Anywhere and Blue Prism as the legacy tools it replaces. No source shows them acquiring Automat as of the November 2025 Series A.

market_need_then: Legacy RPA is described by the company as slow, expensive and fragile. Large language models and vision models in 2022 and 2023 made text-to-action automation newly possible, which the founders cited as the opening after working on robotics at Google X.

branding.domain_note: Operates at runautomat.com rather than an exact automat.com match (site seen in 2026).

identity.mascot_or_character: Ace, the AI teammate with its own profile image, email, phone and logins (Workforce product)
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, confident and plainspoken, short declarative sentences, frames AI as a coworker (homepage seen 2026)

rebrands.why: Not stated by the company; one profile ties the rename to the September 2023 seed announcement and a broader mission beyond workflows. CB Insights lists the company as formerly Lasso.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself or community found. The Ace character is a distinctive product framing, but the name Automat is a generic real word and the company reports mainly enterprise sales.

pivots.from: Lasso, RPA for Chrome using GPT-3 and computer vision
pivots.to: Automat, managed agentic automation for enterprises, later the Ace digital teammate (Workforce)
pivots.why: Mission expanded from browser workflows to operating the whole computer, per one profile. Not confirmed by the company.

outcome_analysis: Automat is active and has raised about $19.25M, ending with a $15.5M Series A led by Felicis in November 2025. It rode the LLM and vision model wave to attack legacy RPA, and the forward-deployed engineering model suggests an enterprise sales motion. Customer counts and revenue are not public, so product market fit cannot be measured from sources. It remains early with no exit.
notes: Seed date is September 2023 per aggregators and one profile; the CMU article gives the amount but no date, so only the year is recorded. Total raised $19.25M per the company blog matches 3.75 plus 15.5. One aggregator showing $23.3M total was ignored. An unrelated 2017 conversational platform also called Automat appears in search results and was excluded.
